footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines (−$608M in 2025). From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $143M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 5.6% to $8.2B in 2025. Net interest income rose 3.9% to $5.9B and noninterest income rose 10.0% to $2.4B; noninterest expense rose 1.5%, and the provision for credit losses was $0, versus $0.
Net income to common rose 23.0% to $1.7B, or $3.86 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 64.4% versus 67.0%. Citizens returned $1.4B through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 23.0% to $1.7B.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: Citizens Financial Group, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
